---
title: Environment Variables
---

There are a few ways for you to read in an environment variable.
For individual projects,
the convension is to use a `.env` (R/Python) or `.Renviron` (R) file.
These files are typically ignored in the `.gitignore`

:::{.callout-important}
DO **NOT** commit your environment variable files into the repository.
Espeically if you have a password or API key in them.
:::

For global environment variables, you can use your `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc` file,
but the below packages will override these variables.

## Python

<https://github.com/theskumar/python-dotenv>

```
pip install python-dotenv
```

Create a `.env` file with `KEY=VALUE` pairs

```python
import os

from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()  # reads variables from a .env file and sets them in os.environ
```

You then use it with `os.environ['YOUR_KEY']`

## R

CRAN also has a `dotenv` package: <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dotenv/index.html>

You can also use the `.Renviron` file that will be read when R loads up
(<https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/ide/guide/environments/r/managing-r.html>).
